lider.eyebrow: Who is on the other side
lider.title: Hello, I'm {leader_name}.
lider.fallback_bio: I'm an independent Oriflame partner, and I don't speak for the brand. I help people who want to get to know the products, pay less for what they already use, or start something of their own. Before anyone decides anything, I prefer to lay it all out clearly: the terms, what is involved and what you can realistically expect. If you still have questions after the assessment, get in touch. You'll hear back from me, with no rush and no pressure.

items.a: The assessment is free. Sign-up terms are set by Oriflame and differ from country to country; {leader_name} will show you all of them before you sign up, including what costs something and what does not. There is no obligation to buy stock.

items.q: Do I have to sell, or bring other people in?
items.a: No. You can sign up just to buy for yourself. Sharing the products is your choice, and inviting others is optional: you don't need to do it to buy at a discount or to sell. In Oriflame's plan, earnings come from product orders, not from signing people up.

items.q: Is this the official Oriflame shop?
items.a: No. Atelier Nórdico is an independent Oriflame partner. The products, orders, prices and terms are Oriflame's; the support comes from {leader_name}.

items.q: Are the numbers in the assessment guaranteed?
items.a: No, and that is why we call it a simulation. It comes from your answers, the member discount Oriflame publishes for your country and assumptions we show in full. Team bonuses are left out of the calculation. Real results depend on your time and your sales.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: As much as you have. The assessment asks how many hours a week you can give it and adjusts the scenarios to match. If you only want to buy, it takes no time at all.
It is used to send you the report and, if you ask, for {leader_name} to reply to you. It is never sold or shared for advertising. You can ask to see it or have it deleted at any time, under UK GDPR.

items.q: Can I do this from another country?
items.a: The assessment works for Portugal, Spain, France and the United Kingdom. Each country has its own terms, and the calculation takes the country you choose into account.

Yes. It is an independent, self-employed activity, not an employment contract, with the tax obligations that apply in your country. {leader_name} can walk you through the first steps; for your own situation, it is best to speak to an accountant.

cta_final.title: 3 minutes to find out, not to decide.
cta_final.text: Look at your numbers in your own time. The decision is still yours, today or later on.

consumidora.label: Buying for yourself, at a discount
consumidora.analysis: From your answers, what you are after is simple: to keep using the products you like and to pay less for them. That is a complete option in its own right, not a compulsory first step towards something else. With the partner discount, part of what you already spend on beauty each month would stay with you, and the simulation shows what that could add up to over a year, based on the spending you mentioned. If, over time, one or two people close to you ask you to order for them too, you can, and that could help cover part of your own spending. But you don't have to, now or later. There are no targets to meet and no obligation to buy stock. The most useful thing in the first few weeks is to browse the catalogue at your own pace, try the products you already use and compare them with what you paid before. Real figures depend on Oriflame's official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, not a commitment.

rendimento_extra.label: A little extra, at your own pace
rendimento_extra.analysis: You told us you are looking for a little extra income that fits into the life you already have, and this analysis was made with that in mind. The hours per week and the contacts you mentioned weigh most in the result, more than enthusiasm or someone else's example. So treat the likely scenario as your reference point and the cautious one as a realistic starting point. The main lever is not constantly finding new customers, but having customers who order again. Two or three happy, well-looked-after people are worth more than lots of one-off conversations. In the first few months it is normal to move slowly, while you get to know the products and build a short, regular routine. Sharing is always your choice, with people you already know and at your own pace, and you can stop whenever you like. Remember that this is a simulation: real results depend on your time, your sales and the official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, not a commitment.

construtora_negocio.label: Building a business of your own
construtora_negocio.analysis: You chose to build a business, and the first thing to understand is where the potential lies: less in your own sales and more in building a team, meaning inviting people and helping them sell well. Not everyone you invite will want to sell, and that is normal. Your sales experience and the way you use social media can speed that process up, but they cannot replace it. It is worth being clear about the start: the first few months are usually slow, because you are building a customer base, learning the plan and supporting your first team members. The simulation reflects that gradual start, and the ambitious scenario only makes sense if the team grows steadily. Building a team is about support, not persuasion: the right people stay when they see a method and honesty. {leader_name} works alongside you from day one. Real results depend on your work and on the official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, not a commitment.
